messages:
Aisha: Quick share — ran continuous-batching grid across A100/H100 in us-west1 and eu-west1. Attaching rough numbers; want feedback before I fold into the onboarding doc.

Carlos: Can you paste p50/p95 and tokens/s for the main configs?

Aisha: Short summary (sampler seq_len=1024, model=redwood-13b-qlo):
- A100 / us-west1: p50=42ms, p95=98ms, tokens/s=2.8k
- H100 / us-west1: p50=31ms, p95=78ms, tokens/s=4.4k
- A100 / eu-west1: p50=45ms, p95=110ms, tokens/s=2.6k
- H100 / eu-west1: p50=33ms, p95=84ms, tokens/s=4.1k

Priya: How did you configure the batch_window and max_batch_tokens?

Aisha: Default grid run used: batch_window_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, min_batch_tokens=32, max_batch_size=32. Noticed tail spikes on H100 when batch_window_ms > 12 — traced to kernel selection flipping (triton vs cutlass). For stable tails we used kernel_pref=["cutlass","triton"].

Jae: Can you drop the scheduler config you used?

Aisha: Pasted minimal scheduler config below (using single quotes in the snippet to keep this readable):
```
{'scheduler': 'continuous', 'batch_window_ms': 8, 'max_batch_tokens': 4096, 'min_batch_tokens': 32, 'max_batch_size': 32, 'fairness': {'mode': 'weighted', 'weights': [{'priority': 'interactive', 'weight': 1.0}, {'priority': 'background', 'weight': 0.2}]}, 'kernel_pref': ['cutlass','triton']}
```

Carlos: Did you try adaptive windowing (auto-expand/shrink)? What about tenant-level knobs?

Aisha: Yes — adaptive windowing reduced p95 by ~12% on A100 under uniform traffic, but it increased variance for low-traffic tenants (small tenants got starved). Mitigation: per-tenant min_batch_tokens + min_window_ms. Example per-tenant policy snippet:
```
per_tenant: { 'min_batch_tokens': 16, 'max_batch_tokens': 2048, 'min_window_ms': 4 }
```

benchmark-bot: Auto-bench summary uploaded: https://ci.redwood/bench/1718654321 (contains raw traces, flamegraphs, kernel switches)

Priya: Any quality regressions with quantized kernels or different kernel paths?

Aisha: Quantization notes: q4f32 showed no eval regression on our 1k promptset. q3bfp16 had a few long-context hallucinations in 3/1000 cases so we rolled that back. Kernel-wise, cutlass path preserved logits better than triton fused on H100 for our ld-attention tests.

Jae: Fairness — how are you weighting interactive vs background? If interactive gets 1.0 and background 0.2 that could starve batch packing for background jobs at low load. Any simulation numbers?

Aisha: We ran micro-sim with 200 tenants (80% background traffic). With weights 1.0/0.2 background tail latency grew 3.5x at 95th under low load. Setting background weight to 0.5 + per-tenant min_batch_tokens removed starvation and only increased interactive p95 by ~6%. Will add a hedging rule for stuck requests.

Carlos: Please add plots: tokens/s vs batch_window for seq_len=512 and 1024, and a kernel-switch heatmap (window vs seq_len) that shows when we pick cutlass vs triton.

Aisha: On it — also note region diff: eu-west1 A100 had slightly higher p95 (~10%) due to network jitter on our test harness. Need to sanity-check instance placement (RDMA vs default).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of scheduler changes (batch_window_ms=8, kernel_pref cutlass-first) to us-west1-small-pool started — watch p95 and kernel-switch logs. :rocket:

Priya: Nice. One more ask — include a short regression checklist for new model onboarding (kernel smoke, quant eval, batch-window sweep, per-region sanity).

Aisha: Will add checklist + baseline artifact links in the onboarding doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
